english.title: Intentionally obstruct a person lawfully acting as an enforcement agent
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) intentionally obstructed **(..SPECIFY PERSON..), who was lawfully acting as an enforcement agent authorised by section 63(2) of the Tribunals, Courts and Enforcement Act 2007
english.legislation: Contrary to paragraph 68(1) of Schedule 12 to the Tribunals, Courts and Enforcement Act 2007.
english.pointstoprove:
Date and Location
intentionally obstruct

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: The definition of an 'enforcement agent' can be found in section 63 of the Act.
english.standardstatementoffacts: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) the defendant intentionally obstructed **(..SPECIFY PERSON..), who was lawfully acting as an enforcement agent authorised by section 63(2) of the Tribunals, Courts and Enforcement Act 2007, by **(..SPECIFY THE NATURE OF THE OBSTRUCTION..).

other.penalty:
Summary: Fifty-one weeks imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level four on the standard scale

Note: In relation to an offence committed before the commencement of section 281(5) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003, the reference to '51 weeks' is to be read as a reference to '6 months'.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months
